subject: Design review: GPU grid burst model, QoS tiers and egress consolidation for private deployment
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@greenfield.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nick Powell <nick.powell@greenfield.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity targets + burst/QoS questions for private GPU grid

Hi Ethan,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. We've pulled together initial requirements for our on-prem deployment and have a few questions before we finalize the order of magnitude: 

- Sustained throughput target: 1.8M tokens/min during US peak (08:00-20:00 PST)
- Burst allowance: 3x sustained for up to 15 minutes, up to twice per day
- Preferred latency P95: <= 220ms for simple completions (<= 512 tokens)
- We need network egress consolidated through a single NAT pair and limited to 3 Gbps max (per availability zone)

Attached: greenfield_capacity_reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet) and a rough egress map. Can you confirm whether the grid burst model you proposed supports the burst window and the egress cap without overflowing our shared interconnect? Also: any guidance on QoS tiers so we can assign priority to interactive vs batch workloads?

Appreciate it — Samira

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Nick Powell <nick.powell@greenfield.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity targets + burst/QoS questions for private GPU grid

Samira — thanks, this is helpful. High-level answers up front: yes, the grid burst model can support 3x bursts for short windows if engineered with a combination of warm spare allocation and request-level admission control; egress consolidation at 3 Gbps is reasonable but requires two things:

1) careful routing to avoid burst amplification (ensure prefix-cache hits are high, avoid reloading KV for repeated requests), and
2) a QoS shaping layer at the VPC egress so we can throttle lower-priority batch jobs during interactive peaks.

I'll loop in Dylan (runtime) and Lauren (dedicated capacity/product) — they have the tactical sizing math and the policy knobs. I'll propose a short call this afternoon to sync on numbers.

Ethan

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity targets + burst/QoS questions for private GPU grid

Adding the runtime perspective and a quick back-of-envelope: 

- Baseline: to hit 1.8M tokens/min sustained with our typical gptx-small-ish kernels (quantized), expect ~12 GPUs per availability zone assuming 75% effective utilization and usual batching heuristics.
- Burst sizing: to allow 3x for 15 minutes, we can handle it by one of three approaches (sorted by preferred order):
  1) Warm spare fleet: +18 GPUs (1.5x baseline) kept warm (low-cost reservation) to instantaneously accept requests.
  2) Rapid scale with overcommit + cold-start prefetch (complex and adds latency risk).
  3) Cross-AZ spill with prioritized traffic (requires higher egress and may expose interconnect bottlenecks).
- Egress math: if average token payload per request is 1.5 KB, at 3x burst our egress would be ~8.1 Gbps edge-to-internet unless we perform response compression and aggressive prefix/KV caching. To keep to 3 Gbps we need >60% reduction from naive flows (compression + cache + batching).

Action items for today's call:
- Lauren: provide committed SLA tiers and whether warm spare capacity can be offered as a paid buffer.
- Camila: network recommendations (NAT sizing, egress shaping).
- Ethan: map pricing/contract language around warm spares.

Dylan

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira@greenfield.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity targets + burst/QoS questions for private GPU grid

Thanks — quick commercial/tactical note before our call:

- We can offer a Warm Spare tier (billed monthly) that keeps a buffer at idle for instantaneous bursts. For Greenfield's numbers I'd recommend a 1.25x buffer as a starting point (adds ~25% to committed monthly capacity) while we validate traffic patterns for 60 days. If you want strict 3x for every burst window we'd need 1.5x warm spare which is costlier but available.
- QoS tiers: Standard (best-effort), Interactive (P95 latency target), and Batch (low-cost, preemptible). Interactive gets priority in request admission and preemption protection on GPUs.
- Network: we can integrate egress shaping rules into the customer's NAT gateway; Camila will provide knobs.

Let's use the 15:00 call to finalize the warm-spare delta and the SLA wording.

Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Head of Dedicated Capacity, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Capacity targets + burst/QoS questions for private GPU grid

Samira/Nick — thanks for the quick sync today. Summary and next steps: 

Summary:
- Sustained 1.8M tokens/min looks like ~12 GPUs/AZ baseline; recommended starting buffer: +25% warm spare (trial 60d).
- For predictable 3x bursts we'd recommend moving to 1.5x warm spare; alternate: cross-AZ spill but that increases egress risk.
- To respect 3 Gbps egress cap we will: compress responses, enable aggressive prefix/KV caching, and apply egress shaping at the NAT (Camila will supply the policy knobs). Expect to achieve ~65%-75% reduction in naive egress when these are active.

Action items:
1) Camila: share egress shaping config and NAT sizing by EOD Thu (attachment: egress_topology_diagram.png).
2) Lauren: send warm-spare pricing tiers and contract language for a 60-day validation trial.
3) Dylan: deliver a one-page ops playbook for burst admission & preemption flow.
4) Ethan: assemble a short SLA appendix draft reflecting Interactive and Batch QoS tiers (attached: qos_sla_draft.pdf).

Samira — once we have the above we can finalize the order and schedule the initial provisioning.

Thanks,
Ethan
